Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 15, verse 1–15 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 1 to 15

Alif. Lam. Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Quran (15:1). That is, these letters, and others like them, are in fact the Quran and the Book of God. These letters are within the reach of all human beings. Yet these same letters take the form of the great signs of God in the Quran. They move beyond the reach of ordinary people and take the form of such constructions and sentences that it is not possible for anyone to bring a speech like it. These letters have no intrinsic meaning of their own, yet in the Quran they become the explanation, the clarifier and the revealer.

Some people today deny these signs and miracles and do not accept the clear Quran, but a day is coming when they will say, with great regret, that how good it would have been had they not adopted this attitude, and that how good it would have been had they believed and remained steadfast.

Perhaps those who have disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims (15:2). That is, a time may come when those who have refused today to accept the call of Islam will, filled with remorse, say: "If only we had submitted!"

That time is not far off, but at that time their wishes will not benefit them. In this manner of expression, they are both mocked in a very subtle way and warned. It is also indicated that the period of respite after the call of Islam presented to you is very limited; do not waste it. Very soon such circumstances will come that these people will wish that they had become Muslims, but at that time these desires will be of no benefit to them.

Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon come to know (15:3). Leave them in the state they are in; they are living merely like animals: eating, drinking and indulging, with no reflection in it. They do not wish to see beyond animal existence, so leave them to their own condition. They have made long and wide plans about this life based on false hopes, while the moments of life are ticking away and opportunities are coming to an end. So leave such people to their own state; their end is going to be bad. Do not become a partner in their activities, O Prophet (ﷺ). These people are immersed in the faithless desires of the world. They are running merely after the mirage of desires. These desires deceive them into thinking that the span of life is still long, and that in this life they will carry out their long and broad plans, that no obstacle will stand before them, that nothing will go against their wishes, and that no one will call them to account for life, and that as they are eating and drinking now, so in the Hereafter or in the coming days of life they will also be successful.

This picture of hopes that deceive like a mirage, and of running in the wilderness after a mirage, is in truth a picture of living human conduct, which is clearly visible in human life and always deceives humanity. A human being always runs after the mirage of these hopes. He remains absorbed in them until he suddenly crosses the limits of peace and well-being, heedless of God, heedless of death, ignorant of the decrees of destiny and fate, heedless of his duties, leaping over the limits of the lawful and the unlawful, until he becomes heedless even of God. He does not think of death and resurrection, and then he is suddenly seized.

This is the state of delusion in which they are involved, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is told to leave them immersed in it. They will soon come to know the real truth, but at that time their knowledge will not benefit them, because their appointed time will have passed. This is a manner of speech that is both threatening and, at the same time, a nudge to awaken them, perhaps they will wake from their intoxication, due to which they are heedless of the very firm evil end. The system of this universe runs according to a specific Sunnah of God. There is no possibility of deviation in this Sunnah. The rise and fall of nations accords exactly with this Sunnah. The end of nations is determined according to the attitude they adopt regarding this Sunnah of God.

We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree (15:4). No people can be destroyed before their appointed time, nor can they be spared after it (15:5). So if someone has been granted some respite and the punishment has been delayed, they should not become heedless. The punishment coming early or late is in accordance with the Sunnah of God, but they will soon come to know.

Who grants respite to nations? It is in the power of God, and the determination of respite or punishment is in accordance with the conduct of people. If someone believes, adopts the path of goodness, corrects his conduct and establishes a system of justice and fairness in the world, then the respite is extended. But when that nation adopts immorality and evil paths, the amount of goodness in it diminishes and no good is expected from it. Then that community reaches its appointed end, and its existence is wiped out from this world. Either it is completely annihilated, or it is reduced to such weakness that its existence is regarded as non-existent.

It may be asked: some nations are neither believers, nor righteous, nor pious, and there is no justice among them, yet despite this they are rising in the world, are powerful and mighty, and continue to survive. This question appears strong on the surface, but it is not correct, because the nations which give rise to this question necessarily possessed some aspects of goodness and righteousness. For example, they discharge the duty of God's vicegerency on earth well, they do good work in the cultivation and building of the world, and in the regions where they live they practise justice, although their concept of justice is limited. They have established a standard of material progress and material welfare, although it is based on a limited outlook. These nations are receiving this respite only because of this limited good in them. Whenever that good ends, these nations will end.

The truth is that there is no possibility of deviation in the Sunnah of God. For the decline of every community and every nation there is an appointed time, and it occurs at its time.

No community can outstrip its term, nor can it lag behind (15:5). No nation should be proud of the fact that God's grip has not yet seized them. Here, within the context of the discourse, a glimpse of their evil attitude towards the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is also shown, although the Messenger has placed before them a clear Book. It awakens them and reminds them of a lesson they have forgotten. It gives them new light, but they mock it in reverse and go to extremes in misguidance.

They say: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad! If you are truthful, why do you not bring us the angels?" (15:6–7). They said this sentence to the Messenger (ﷺ): "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed."

They used "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed" as a mockery, because in reality these people denied the revelation of prophethood. They used this phrase in a tone of arrogance and derision. Moreover, their attitude towards the Messenger (ﷺ) was so insolent that they used for him the words "you are surely mad" (15:6), and they called him mad because he was continually calling them to the faith. These people also demanded from the Messenger (ﷺ) the descent of angels, which they did as an extreme form of mockery.

"Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?" (15:7). The demand from deniers for the descent of angels is repeated again and again in this surah and in other surahs. This demand has been made of you and of other messengers, and those who made this demand have neither recognised the human being nor realised in their hearts his true worth, that God has bestowed the station of prophethood upon a human being, and has sent chosen people from among humanity as prophets.

The Quran answers this question by saying that it is not the office of angels to assist the messengers in their preaching. Angels come to assist the messengers when the proof of preaching has been completed and, in accordance with the Sunnah of God, the decision is made that the deniers are now to be destroyed. Their period of respite has ended. When the angels come at that time, the respite has already come to an end.

We do not send down the angels except with truth, and then they would not be granted respite (15:8). Do these people want such a descent of angels, and is this what they demand?

After describing the danger of this demand, before them is placed the invitation to adopt the attitude of guidance, intellect and reflection, and it is said that the angels come with truth, and when they come they carry out the execution of truth, and the deniers deserve to be annihilated. So when the angels descend, they come for the execution of that final, true decision. That the angels are not descending upon them is good for them, but they cannot understand their own good. God is sending down upon them verses of remembrance and reflection, instead of angels, so that they may ponder, reflect and not invite their own destruction. For them, the non-descent of angels is better.

Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians (15:9). So for them the best course is to accept it. This final advice is preserved and will remain until eternity. It contains truth, with no admixture of falsehood. No distortion can now be made in it. And this final advice is sufficient to guide them in every matter of life, provided they seek the truth and do not make the wrong demand for the descent of angels, because God has not yet decided to send angels. Because God still desires their good, instead of sending angels to destroy them, He has sent down the Quran preserved.

Now the Messenger (ﷺ) is also consoled in his own place. It is told that he is not the first messenger to be received with denial and mockery; messengers have come among earlier nations as well, and they too were denied and mocked just as you were.

And We did send messengers before you among the earlier peoples (15:10). No messenger ever came to a people without their mocking him (15:11). It is said that, O Muhammad (ﷺ), just as those addressed by the earlier prophets treated the call they presented, exactly so these deniers are treating the call you present, and in this way We cast this call into their hearts, while their hearts neither wish to ponder it nor are they ready to accept it.

Thus We insert it into the hearts of the guilty. They do not believe in it, and the way of the ancients has already passed (15:12–13). It is not that the messengers did not present arguments for these people to reflect upon; rather the real matter is that they are caught in obstinacy and arrogance, and they advance in opposition to faith.

Here an example of their humiliating obstinacy is also presented, and it is shown that they are afflicted with extreme hatred and envy against the call of Islam.

And even if We opened for them a gate into heaven and they continued ascending through it, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled; indeed we have been bewitched" (15:14–15). The mere idea that a human being is rising in the heavens is itself a kind of opening of a gate. But if they were to ascend in their bodies actually, see the gates of the heavens opened before them, see that they are ascending, and their perceiving senses see that this process is taking place, and they witness it, even then they would not be ready to abandon their obstinacy, and they would say: "No, no, this is not reality; rather we have been bewitched, and our sight has been deluded. What we see is mere imagination. Indeed we have been clearly bewitched. Whatever we are witnessing and sensing is all sorcery."

This passage is the second half of Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah al-Hijr (15:1–15) in the Urdu translation. Here is the English rendering:

Thus the Qur'an paints an extremely vivid picture of their obstinacy, through which their base self-interest is made apparent. The purpose is to show that arguing with such people is utterly futile. The aim is to establish that they are not lacking in proofs of faith, and that their demand for the descent of the angels, which is not fulfilled, is a pretext. They do not believe because, even if a means of ascent into the heavens were arranged for them in place of the descent of angels, their attitude would remain the same. They are obstinate to the utmost degree, careless, shameless and audacious. Even if the truth were to come as plainly as the light of day, they would still not be ready to accept it.

Here the Qur'an gives an excellent portrayal of those among humankind who are obstinate. It is so ugly a depiction that a person feels disgust at it and comes to regard the form of these people as exceedingly contemptible.

:::

Now, moving from the scene of obstinacy, we turn to the cosmic signs and proofs. The display of obstinacy related only to the heavens; now the whole universe is set before us. First the heavens are taken up, then certain phenomena of the earth are brought forward. A scene is presented of winds laden with rain-bearing clouds; then the varied forms of life and death on this earth are shown; and after that some scenes of the Gathering and Resurrection. Those who deny all these signs and evidences are the same people who, even if the doors of the heavens were opened for them and they were to ascend through them, would still, out of their obstinacy, not believe, and would say: "Our eyes are being deceived, we have been put under a spell, we have been bewitched." Now, look at all these scenes and witnesses one by one.

Verses 1 to 15

Alif. Lam. Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Quran (15:1). That is, these letters, and others like them, are in fact the Quran and the Book of God. These letters are within the reach of all human beings. Yet these same letters take the form of the great signs of God in the Quran. They move beyond the reach of ordinary people and take the form of such constructions and sentences that it is not possible for anyone to bring a speech like it. These letters have no intrinsic meaning of their own, yet in the Quran they become the explanation, the clarifier and the revealer.

Some people today deny these signs and miracles and do not accept the clear Quran, but a day is coming when they will say, with great regret, that how good it would have been had they not adopted this attitude, and that how good it would have been had they believed and remained steadfast.

Perhaps those who have disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims (15:2). That is, a time may come when those who have refused today to accept the call of Islam will, filled with remorse, say: "If only we had submitted!"

That time is not far off, but at that time their wishes will not benefit them. In this manner of expression, they are both mocked in a very subtle way and warned. It is also indicated that the period of respite after the call of Islam presented to you is very limited; do not waste it. Very soon such circumstances will come that these people will wish that they had become Muslims, but at that time these desires will be of no benefit to them.

Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon come to know (15:3). Leave them in the state they are in; they are living merely like animals: eating, drinking and indulging, with no reflection in it. They do not wish to see beyond animal existence, so leave them to their own condition. They have made long and wide plans about this life based on false hopes, while the moments of life are ticking away and opportunities are coming to an end. So leave such people to their own state; their end is going to be bad. Do not become a partner in their activities, O Prophet (ﷺ). These people are immersed in the faithless desires of the world. They are running merely after the mirage of desires. These desires deceive them into thinking that the span of life is still long, and that in this life they will carry out their long and broad plans, that no obstacle will stand before them, that nothing will go against their wishes, and that no one will call them to account for life, and that as they are eating and drinking now, so in the Hereafter or in the coming days of life they will also be successful.

This picture of hopes that deceive like a mirage, and of running in the wilderness after a mirage, is in truth a picture of living human conduct, which is clearly visible in human life and always deceives humanity. A human being always runs after the mirage of these hopes. He remains absorbed in them until he suddenly crosses the limits of peace and well-being, heedless of God, heedless of death, ignorant of the decrees of destiny and fate, heedless of his duties, leaping over the limits of the lawful and the unlawful, until he becomes heedless even of God. He does not think of death and resurrection, and then he is suddenly seized.

This is the state of delusion in which they are involved, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is told to leave them immersed in it. They will soon come to know the real truth, but at that time their knowledge will not benefit them, because their appointed time will have passed. This is a manner of speech that is both threatening and, at the same time, a nudge to awaken them, perhaps they will wake from their intoxication, due to which they are heedless of the very firm evil end. The system of this universe runs according to a specific Sunnah of God. There is no possibility of deviation in this Sunnah. The rise and fall of nations accords exactly with this Sunnah. The end of nations is determined according to the attitude they adopt regarding this Sunnah of God.

We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree (15:4). No people can be destroyed before their appointed time, nor can they be spared after it (15:5). So if someone has been granted some respite and the punishment has been delayed, they should not become heedless. The punishment coming early or late is in accordance with the Sunnah of God, but they will soon come to know.

Who grants respite to nations? It is in the power of God, and the determination of respite or punishment is in accordance with the conduct of people. If someone believes, adopts the path of goodness, corrects his conduct and establishes a system of justice and fairness in the world, then the respite is extended. But when that nation adopts immorality and evil paths, the amount of goodness in it diminishes and no good is expected from it. Then that community reaches its appointed end, and its existence is wiped out from this world. Either it is completely annihilated, or it is reduced to such weakness that its existence is regarded as non-existent.

It may be asked: some nations are neither believers, nor righteous, nor pious, and there is no justice among them, yet despite this they are rising in the world, are powerful and mighty, and continue to survive. This question appears strong on the surface, but it is not correct, because the nations which give rise to this question necessarily possessed some aspects of goodness and righteousness. For example, they discharge the duty of God's vicegerency on earth well, they do good work in the cultivation and building of the world, and in the regions where they live they practise justice, although their concept of justice is limited. They have established a standard of material progress and material welfare, although it is based on a limited outlook. These nations are receiving this respite only because of this limited good in them. Whenever that good ends, these nations will end.

The truth is that there is no possibility of deviation in the Sunnah of God. For the decline of every community and every nation there is an appointed time, and it occurs at its time.

No community can outstrip its term, nor can it lag behind (15:5). No nation should be proud of the fact that God's grip has not yet seized them. Here, within the context of the discourse, a glimpse of their evil attitude towards the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is also shown, although the Messenger has placed before them a clear Book. It awakens them and reminds them of a lesson they have forgotten. It gives them new light, but they mock it in reverse and go to extremes in misguidance.

They say: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad! If you are truthful, why do you not bring us the angels?" (15:6–7). They said this sentence to the Messenger (ﷺ): "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed."

They used "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed" as a mockery, because in reality these people denied the revelation of prophethood. They used this phrase in a tone of arrogance and derision. Moreover, their attitude towards the Messenger (ﷺ) was so insolent that they used for him the words "you are surely mad" (15:6), and they called him mad because he was continually calling them to the faith. These people also demanded from the Messenger (ﷺ) the descent of angels, which they did as an extreme form of mockery.

"Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?" (15:7). The demand from deniers for the descent of angels is repeated again and again in this surah and in other surahs. This demand has been made of you and of other messengers, and those who made this demand have neither recognised the human being nor realised in their hearts his true worth, that God has bestowed the station of prophethood upon a human being, and has sent chosen people from among humanity as prophets.

The Quran answers this question by saying that it is not the office of angels to assist the messengers in their preaching. Angels come to assist the messengers when the proof of preaching has been completed and, in accordance with the Sunnah of God, the decision is made that the deniers are now to be destroyed. Their period of respite has ended. When the angels come at that time, the respite has already come to an end.

We do not send down the angels except with truth, and then they would not be granted respite (15:8). Do these people want such a descent of angels, and is this what they demand?

After describing the danger of this demand, before them is placed the invitation to adopt the attitude of guidance, intellect and reflection, and it is said that the angels come with truth, and when they come they carry out the execution of truth, and the deniers deserve to be annihilated. So when the angels descend, they come for the execution of that final, true decision. That the angels are not descending upon them is good for them, but they cannot understand their own good. God is sending down upon them verses of remembrance and reflection, instead of angels, so that they may ponder, reflect and not invite their own destruction. For them, the non-descent of angels is better.

Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians (15:9). So for them the best course is to accept it. This final advice is preserved and will remain until eternity. It contains truth, with no admixture of falsehood. No distortion can now be made in it. And this final advice is sufficient to guide them in every matter of life, provided they seek the truth and do not make the wrong demand for the descent of angels, because God has not yet decided to send angels. Because God still desires their good, instead of sending angels to destroy them, He has sent down the Quran preserved.

Now the Messenger (ﷺ) is also consoled in his own place. It is told that he is not the first messenger to be received with denial and mockery; messengers have come among earlier nations as well, and they too were denied and mocked just as you were.

And We did send messengers before you among the earlier peoples (15:10). No messenger ever came to a people without their mocking him (15:11). It is said that, O Muhammad (ﷺ), just as those addressed by the earlier prophets treated the call they presented, exactly so these deniers are treating the call you present, and in this way We cast this call into their hearts, while their hearts neither wish to ponder it nor are they ready to accept it.

Thus We insert it into the hearts of the guilty. They do not believe in it, and the way of the ancients has already passed (15:12–13). It is not that the messengers did not present arguments for these people to reflect upon; rather the real matter is that they are caught in obstinacy and arrogance, and they advance in opposition to faith.

Here an example of their humiliating obstinacy is also presented, and it is shown that they are afflicted with extreme hatred and envy against the call of Islam.

And even if We opened for them a gate into heaven and they continued ascending through it, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled; indeed we have been bewitched" (15:14–15). The mere idea that a human being is rising in the heavens is itself a kind of opening of a gate. But if they were to ascend in their bodies actually, see the gates of the heavens opened before them, see that they are ascending, and their perceiving senses see that this process is taking place, and they witness it, even then they would not be ready to abandon their obstinacy, and they would say: "No, no, this is not reality; rather we have been bewitched, and our sight has been deluded. What we see is mere imagination. Indeed we have been clearly bewitched. Whatever we are witnessing and sensing is all sorcery."

This passage is the second half of Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah al-Hijr (15:1–15) in the Urdu translation. Here is the English rendering:

Thus the Qur'an paints an extremely vivid picture of their obstinacy, through which their base self-interest is made apparent. The purpose is to show that arguing with such people is utterly futile. The aim is to establish that they are not lacking in proofs of faith, and that their demand for the descent of the angels, which is not fulfilled, is a pretext. They do not believe because, even if a means of ascent into the heavens were arranged for them in place of the descent of angels, their attitude would remain the same. They are obstinate to the utmost degree, careless, shameless and audacious. Even if the truth were to come as plainly as the light of day, they would still not be ready to accept it.

Here the Qur'an gives an excellent portrayal of those among humankind who are obstinate. It is so ugly a depiction that a person feels disgust at it and comes to regard the form of these people as exceedingly contemptible.

:::

Now, moving from the scene of obstinacy, we turn to the cosmic signs and proofs. The display of obstinacy related only to the heavens; now the whole universe is set before us. First the heavens are taken up, then certain phenomena of the earth are brought forward. A scene is presented of winds laden with rain-bearing clouds; then the varied forms of life and death on this earth are shown; and after that some scenes of the Gathering and Resurrection. Those who deny all these signs and evidences are the same people who, even if the doors of the heavens were opened for them and they were to ascend through them, would still, out of their obstinacy, not believe, and would say: "Our eyes are being deceived, we have been put under a spell, we have been bewitched." Now, look at all these scenes and witnesses one by one.

Verses 1 to 15

Alif. Lam. Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Quran (15:1). That is, these letters, and others like them, are in fact the Quran and the Book of God. These letters are within the reach of all human beings. Yet these same letters take the form of the great signs of God in the Quran. They move beyond the reach of ordinary people and take the form of such constructions and sentences that it is not possible for anyone to bring a speech like it. These letters have no intrinsic meaning of their own, yet in the Quran they become the explanation, the clarifier and the revealer.

Some people today deny these signs and miracles and do not accept the clear Quran, but a day is coming when they will say, with great regret, that how good it would have been had they not adopted this attitude, and that how good it would have been had they believed and remained steadfast.

Perhaps those who have disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims (15:2). That is, a time may come when those who have refused today to accept the call of Islam will, filled with remorse, say: "If only we had submitted!"

That time is not far off, but at that time their wishes will not benefit them. In this manner of expression, they are both mocked in a very subtle way and warned. It is also indicated that the period of respite after the call of Islam presented to you is very limited; do not waste it. Very soon such circumstances will come that these people will wish that they had become Muslims, but at that time these desires will be of no benefit to them.

Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon come to know (15:3). Leave them in the state they are in; they are living merely like animals: eating, drinking and indulging, with no reflection in it. They do not wish to see beyond animal existence, so leave them to their own condition. They have made long and wide plans about this life based on false hopes, while the moments of life are ticking away and opportunities are coming to an end. So leave such people to their own state; their end is going to be bad. Do not become a partner in their activities, O Prophet (ﷺ). These people are immersed in the faithless desires of the world. They are running merely after the mirage of desires. These desires deceive them into thinking that the span of life is still long, and that in this life they will carry out their long and broad plans, that no obstacle will stand before them, that nothing will go against their wishes, and that no one will call them to account for life, and that as they are eating and drinking now, so in the Hereafter or in the coming days of life they will also be successful.

This picture of hopes that deceive like a mirage, and of running in the wilderness after a mirage, is in truth a picture of living human conduct, which is clearly visible in human life and always deceives humanity. A human being always runs after the mirage of these hopes. He remains absorbed in them until he suddenly crosses the limits of peace and well-being, heedless of God, heedless of death, ignorant of the decrees of destiny and fate, heedless of his duties, leaping over the limits of the lawful and the unlawful, until he becomes heedless even of God. He does not think of death and resurrection, and then he is suddenly seized.

This is the state of delusion in which they are involved, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is told to leave them immersed in it. They will soon come to know the real truth, but at that time their knowledge will not benefit them, because their appointed time will have passed. This is a manner of speech that is both threatening and, at the same time, a nudge to awaken them, perhaps they will wake from their intoxication, due to which they are heedless of the very firm evil end. The system of this universe runs according to a specific Sunnah of God. There is no possibility of deviation in this Sunnah. The rise and fall of nations accords exactly with this Sunnah. The end of nations is determined according to the attitude they adopt regarding this Sunnah of God.

We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree (15:4). No people can be destroyed before their appointed time, nor can they be spared after it (15:5). So if someone has been granted some respite and the punishment has been delayed, they should not become heedless. The punishment coming early or late is in accordance with the Sunnah of God, but they will soon come to know.

Who grants respite to nations? It is in the power of God, and the determination of respite or punishment is in accordance with the conduct of people. If someone believes, adopts the path of goodness, corrects his conduct and establishes a system of justice and fairness in the world, then the respite is extended. But when that nation adopts immorality and evil paths, the amount of goodness in it diminishes and no good is expected from it. Then that community reaches its appointed end, and its existence is wiped out from this world. Either it is completely annihilated, or it is reduced to such weakness that its existence is regarded as non-existent.

It may be asked: some nations are neither believers, nor righteous, nor pious, and there is no justice among them, yet despite this they are rising in the world, are powerful and mighty, and continue to survive. This question appears strong on the surface, but it is not correct, because the nations which give rise to this question necessarily possessed some aspects of goodness and righteousness. For example, they discharge the duty of God's vicegerency on earth well, they do good work in the cultivation and building of the world, and in the regions where they live they practise justice, although their concept of justice is limited. They have established a standard of material progress and material welfare, although it is based on a limited outlook. These nations are receiving this respite only because of this limited good in them. Whenever that good ends, these nations will end.

The truth is that there is no possibility of deviation in the Sunnah of God. For the decline of every community and every nation there is an appointed time, and it occurs at its time.

No community can outstrip its term, nor can it lag behind (15:5). No nation should be proud of the fact that God's grip has not yet seized them. Here, within the context of the discourse, a glimpse of their evil attitude towards the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is also shown, although the Messenger has placed before them a clear Book. It awakens them and reminds them of a lesson they have forgotten. It gives them new light, but they mock it in reverse and go to extremes in misguidance.

They say: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad! If you are truthful, why do you not bring us the angels?" (15:6–7). They said this sentence to the Messenger (ﷺ): "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed."

They used "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed" as a mockery, because in reality these people denied the revelation of prophethood. They used this phrase in a tone of arrogance and derision. Moreover, their attitude towards the Messenger (ﷺ) was so insolent that they used for him the words "you are surely mad" (15:6), and they called him mad because he was continually calling them to the faith. These people also demanded from the Messenger (ﷺ) the descent of angels, which they did as an extreme form of mockery.

"Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?" (15:7). The demand from deniers for the descent of angels is repeated again and again in this surah and in other surahs. This demand has been made of you and of other messengers, and those who made this demand have neither recognised the human being nor realised in their hearts his true worth, that God has bestowed the station of prophethood upon a human being, and has sent chosen people from among humanity as prophets.

The Quran answers this question by saying that it is not the office of angels to assist the messengers in their preaching. Angels come to assist the messengers when the proof of preaching has been completed and, in accordance with the Sunnah of God, the decision is made that the deniers are now to be destroyed. Their period of respite has ended. When the angels come at that time, the respite has already come to an end.

We do not send down the angels except with truth, and then they would not be granted respite (15:8). Do these people want such a descent of angels, and is this what they demand?

After describing the danger of this demand, before them is placed the invitation to adopt the attitude of guidance, intellect and reflection, and it is said that the angels come with truth, and when they come they carry out the execution of truth, and the deniers deserve to be annihilated. So when the angels descend, they come for the execution of that final, true decision. That the angels are not descending upon them is good for them, but they cannot understand their own good. God is sending down upon them verses of remembrance and reflection, instead of angels, so that they may ponder, reflect and not invite their own destruction. For them, the non-descent of angels is better.

Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians (15:9). So for them the best course is to accept it. This final advice is preserved and will remain until eternity. It contains truth, with no admixture of falsehood. No distortion can now be made in it. And this final advice is sufficient to guide them in every matter of life, provided they seek the truth and do not make the wrong demand for the descent of angels, because God has not yet decided to send angels. Because God still desires their good, instead of sending angels to destroy them, He has sent down the Quran preserved.

Now the Messenger (ﷺ) is also consoled in his own place. It is told that he is not the first messenger to be received with denial and mockery; messengers have come among earlier nations as well, and they too were denied and mocked just as you were.

And We did send messengers before you among the earlier peoples (15:10). No messenger ever came to a people without their mocking him (15:11). It is said that, O Muhammad (ﷺ), just as those addressed by the earlier prophets treated the call they presented, exactly so these deniers are treating the call you present, and in this way We cast this call into their hearts, while their hearts neither wish to ponder it nor are they ready to accept it.

Thus We insert it into the hearts of the guilty. They do not believe in it, and the way of the ancients has already passed (15:12–13). It is not that the messengers did not present arguments for these people to reflect upon; rather the real matter is that they are caught in obstinacy and arrogance, and they advance in opposition to faith.

Here an example of their humiliating obstinacy is also presented, and it is shown that they are afflicted with extreme hatred and envy against the call of Islam.

And even if We opened for them a gate into heaven and they continued ascending through it, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled; indeed we have been bewitched" (15:14–15). The mere idea that a human being is rising in the heavens is itself a kind of opening of a gate. But if they were to ascend in their bodies actually, see the gates of the heavens opened before them, see that they are ascending, and their perceiving senses see that this process is taking place, and they witness it, even then they would not be ready to abandon their obstinacy, and they would say: "No, no, this is not reality; rather we have been bewitched, and our sight has been deluded. What we see is mere imagination. Indeed we have been clearly bewitched. Whatever we are witnessing and sensing is all sorcery."

This passage is the second half of Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah al-Hijr (15:1–15) in the Urdu translation. Here is the English rendering:

Thus the Qur'an paints an extremely vivid picture of their obstinacy, through which their base self-interest is made apparent. The purpose is to show that arguing with such people is utterly futile. The aim is to establish that they are not lacking in proofs of faith, and that their demand for the descent of the angels, which is not fulfilled, is a pretext. They do not believe because, even if a means of ascent into the heavens were arranged for them in place of the descent of angels, their attitude would remain the same. They are obstinate to the utmost degree, careless, shameless and audacious. Even if the truth were to come as plainly as the light of day, they would still not be ready to accept it.

Here the Qur'an gives an excellent portrayal of those among humankind who are obstinate. It is so ugly a depiction that a person feels disgust at it and comes to regard the form of these people as exceedingly contemptible.

:::

Now, moving from the scene of obstinacy, we turn to the cosmic signs and proofs. The display of obstinacy related only to the heavens; now the whole universe is set before us. First the heavens are taken up, then certain phenomena of the earth are brought forward. A scene is presented of winds laden with rain-bearing clouds; then the varied forms of life and death on this earth are shown; and after that some scenes of the Gathering and Resurrection. Those who deny all these signs and evidences are the same people who, even if the doors of the heavens were opened for them and they were to ascend through them, would still, out of their obstinacy, not believe, and would say: "Our eyes are being deceived, we have been put under a spell, we have been bewitched." Now, look at all these scenes and witnesses one by one.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 16–18:

Verses 16 to 18

This is the first line of this vast expanse of the universe. It is the first picture of the designs of this wondrous universe. In this universe there are marvels greater than even the descent of the angels. The very formation of the universe, and its functioning in terms of natural law, is a clear example of Allah's power and craftsmanship. With it present, there is no need at all for any other proof.

What are the buruj (constellations/mansions)? They are these stars and planets, great and greater still. The orbits and positions of these planets and stars may also be what is meant by buruj. Whatever is meant, in both cases their functioning is a miraculous proof and a just witness to the power and wisdom of Allah; how intricate, how effective, and in appearance also a beautiful scene.

﴿And We have adorned it for the beholders﴾ (15:16). "We adorned it for those who look." Behold the beauty of this whole universe, and especially the beauty of the lowest heaven. This verse shows that in this universe, beyond wisdom and measure, beauty too has been kept in view. Mere vastness is not the aim of this universe; mere immensity is not the aim; it is not merely that attention has been given to its intricate structure, but that a particular beauty has also been kept in view in its structure.

Have you ever, on a beautiful night, raised your gaze to the sky, where the stars lie scattered, each star radiating light, as though it were an ember glowing in its place? Then, in that state, your eye falls upon a star that is extremely distant. Now bring another scene before you. It is a beautiful night, in which the full moon of the fourteenth night stands high, and before it the universe stands in silence.

To feel the beauty of this universe, on a clear night without the moon and on a beautiful night of the full moon, a poetic gaze alone is sufficient. How vast is this beauty? And how deep is its effect upon the veil of feeling? Is any other proof needed beyond this?

﴿And We have adorned it for the beholders﴾ (15:16). "O, for those who behold, We have adorned it." Those who do not behold as well. But along with filling this universe with beauty, it has also been made most protected and pure.

﴿And We protected it from every accursed Satan﴾ (15:17). No satanic power can corrupt it, and no satanic power can pollute its atmosphere. No satanic power can insert its virus into the system of this universe and disturb its order. It cannot defile it, nor can it misguide it by turning aside its course, in the way that Satan carries out all these works upon this earth, and this earth is his mission. On this earth Satan can accomplish his mission, but in the system of the heavens he has no role or influence. Over the heavens and the heights his reach does not extend. His impurities and misguidances can accomplish nothing there. His attacks upon the heavens are turned back; there, arrangements for their defence exist.

﴿Except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾ (15:18). What is Satan, and what is his reality? How does he steal hearing from the heavens, and what does he steal? All these matters relate to the unseen world. We can understand their meaning only to the extent that it is found in these Quranic texts. There is no benefit in further seeking after them, for even if we were to discover something more in this field about how Satan steals hearing, it would have no connection with any increase or decrease in our faith. In these matters, investigation and scrutiny bring harm rather than benefit, for a person turns away from the practical affairs of this life and begins merely to gallop on the horses of the intellect, and yet he cannot attain any new reality or any new knowledge.

What we need to know is this: that Satan has no role or influence in the heavens. This vast universe, its beauty, its movement and its activity, are protected from the reach of Satan. When interference by satanic powers in the affairs of this universe occurs, or an attempt at such interference is made, at that moment the satanic powers are driven away and their designs are halted by the shooting star.

The manner in which lofty fortresses and towers are mentioned here, the way the attempts of the devils to ascend are spoken of, and then the way they are bombarded, is, in terms of imagination, contemplation and observation, a most beautiful scene, and a beautiful example of the artistic depiction of the Qur'an.

The second line of this vast canopy of the universe is the wide earth upon which we dwell. To our eyes it is vaster, long and broad. It is very open for our travel and exploration. Within it are lofty mountains, every kind of vegetation, and fruits and flowers. Moreover, there is abundant provision of sustenance for human beings and all other living creatures.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 19–20:

Verses 19 to 20

There is a kind of expansiveness and grandeur present in the atmospheres of this universe. The heavens are described as containing great fortresses. Even in the pronunciation of the word burooj (the mansions/constellations) there is a certain resonance and majesty. The shihab (shooting star) is described with the word mubeen (clear, manifest), and this points to a sense of grandeur.

On the earth, the mountains are called rawasi (firmly fixed mountains), and the heaviness and massiveness of these mountains is expressed through the word alqaynaa (We cast/threw). Then vegetation is qualified with the attribute mawzoon. Mawzoon is heavy and massive both in its literal and its meaning. Although the intended meaning here is that, by reason of its intricate structure, it is firm and balanced. Then, in this atmosphere of grandeur, instead of the word mu'ishat (livelihood) the word ma'ayish is used, and it has been left indefinite in the form of an indefinite noun (nakirah). Then, in the phrase ﴿man lastum lahu bi-raziqeen﴾ (for whom you are not its providers, 15:20), a reference is also made to all living creatures that exist on this planet. In short, in expressions, words and meanings, in every respect, there is nothing but grandeur in this scene. This is a cosmic verse (ayah takwiniyyah). It passes from the horizons of the universe and also takes in the inner selves (anfus). This vast land which invites contemplation and invites entrustment, these magnificent mountains that rise upon the bosom of the earth, and these various kinds of plants that grow upon it, and then the discourse focuses on the aspect that all of them are for the benefit of human beings. The provision for life on this earth and the many kinds of food, the verse leaves them unspecified so that their vastness and grandeur may be indicated. All of this, O human being, is for you. And then, for your sake, creatures have also been created which are beneficial to you and which you do not sustain. Allah, and Allah alone, sustains them. You are, in this way, a community and a creation, just as other creatures are, whose number and kinds are also unknown to anyone. This diverse creation is nourished by the special provision of Allah. And Allah, O human being, has put them at your service without cost. Then there is a class of creatures that is nourished by the provision of Allah and upon whom no obligations are placed.

All these varieties of creatures and their diverse sustenance, Allah the Exalted has created in full, in full measure, in this universe, and all this creation and its means of subsistence are in the hand of Allah's power and under His sole disposal, and Allah, according to His sunnah (established way), disposes of all affairs as He wills, and causes His commands to take effect within His creation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verse 21:

Verse 21

Therefore, no kind among created beings owns anything. All treasures are under the sovereignty of Allah, they are in the power of Allah's omnipotent hand. Allah sends down whatever treasures He wills for His creation, in a known and determined measure, and nothing is ever sent down (to earth) without a purpose, nor does anything happen by chance.

Among the things which Allah sends down in a known measure are the winds and the rains as well.

Verse 22

Do the winds bear fertilizing burdens? Water, just as Allah causes the clouds to bear water, and then the clouds, which are bearers of water, pour it down from the heavens, and thus We give you water to drink. Are the treasures of rain in your possession, that you may send it down whenever you need? Rather, these treasures are in Allah's possession, and Allah sends it down in a known measure.

These winds blow according to atmospheric laws, and according to those atmospheric regulations water is in them and falls. The question here is: who created these atmospheres, and who established these laws of the winds and rains? It is certainly the work of the Creator of the universe; therefore all these causes and means are in accordance with Allah's universal law and the supreme computer.

"And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasures, and We do not send it down except in a known measure" (15:21). Observe the manner of expression here: every movement, even the giving of drink, is attributed to Allah.

"And We gave you to drink of it" (15:22). Although the meaning is that We created you such that you seek water, and made water such that it fulfils your need, and We balanced this demand and supply. But the manner of expression is one that suits the occasion and context of the discourse. Every action and every movement is attributed to Allah, because the intention is to convey the impression that every movement and every event in this universe occurs by Allah's will and command. The cosmic law Allah has for the heavens is the same for all creatures as well. In the first verse there was a statement about the Divine way regarding the deniers; in this second part, there is a statement about the Divine way regarding the heavens, the earth and the universe, and in this context the system of winds and waters also follows that same way. None of these matters occurs apart from or outside the Divine way. All affairs proceed according to that supreme law which operates in this universe and which the Qur'an calls the Truth.

The subject concludes with this: life and death are also in Allah's power. Giving life to all things, causing them to die, raising them again, and reckoning and accounting are all in Allah's control.

Verses 23–25

This second paragraph is in harmony with the first. The first said:

﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.﴾ (15:23) ﴿And We certainly know those who have gone before you and We certainly know those who will come later.﴾ (15:24) "For every community that We destroyed, a specific term had been written. No nation can be destroyed before its appointed time, nor can it be spared after it." Here, however, it is decided that life and death are in Allah's hand, that Allah is the inheritor of all, and that after death people will be raised to Him. Allah knows, and He has recorded, who will be taken first, who will be granted a term of action, and who will leave this world afterwards. In any case, everyone will be raised after death and will return to Allah.

﴿Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.﴾ (15:25) "He is Wise and Knowing." In accordance with His wisdom, He fixes the respite for nations and individuals. He knows the time of death, He has also determined and fixed the time of the Resurrection, and the affairs of the intervening period are also in His hand.

The movements of the scene are in harmony in this paragraph and in the previous one. The descent of guidance from the heavens, the descent of angels, the bombardment of devils with shooting stars, the blowing of winds and the descent of rain: all these scenes appear in both. Then the great events of this world and the universe, the heavens, fortresses, stars and planets, the earth, mountains, winds, rains and vegetation, are also shared scenes. A similar example, in harmony with the theme of these verses, is given to express obstinacy: if a gate were opened in the sky and these people were to climb into it, their stubbornness and obstinate denial would still be the same. In short, the theme and its pictorial portrayal reveal the unique style of expression of the Great Qur'an.

* * *

Now the great story of the creation of humankind is presented here: the beginning of humanity, the wisdom of guidance and misguidance in this world, and its causes and factors, that is, the story of Adam. From what elements were they created, and in what manner? What were the circumstances at the time of their creation and afterwards?

Previously, in this commentary, we have studied the story of Adam twice, in Surah al-Baqarah (the Cow, chapter 2) and Surah al-A'raf (the Heights, chapter 7). On both occasions the story was narrated in particular circumstances and for particular purposes. That is why different links of the story were brought in each place, and the style of narration was also different. The atmosphere of the story and its effects differed, although some effects and outcomes were identical in both places. This story is now coming a third time.

Some introductory statements of this story are identical in all three places. For example, in Surah al-Baqarah, where the story came, the following was said before it:

﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then turned to the heaven and made it into seven heavens; and He is Knower of all things.﴾ (2:29)

And in Surah al-A'raf (7), where the story came, the following was said before it:

﴿And We have established you upon the earth and provided for you therein means of living; little are you grateful.﴾ (7:10)

And here, in Surah al-Hijr (15:19), it is said:

﴿And the earth We have spread out, and placed therein firm mountains, and caused to grow therein from every kind of thing in a measured balance.﴾ (15:19)

However, the manner of narrating the story is different in these three places, and its purpose and objective are also different.

In Surah al-Baqarah, the purpose of the story was that, after the creation of the universe, Allah appointed Adam (peace be upon him) on this earth as His vicegerent (khalifah), and that all the facilities present within the earth are for the children of Adam. Therefore the narration begins thus:

﴿And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create upon the earth a vicegerent."﴾ (2:30)

So there the secrets and mysteries of Adam's office of earthly vicegerency are explained, at which the angels were astonished, because those secrets were hidden from their view. Accordingly, Allah had to reveal to them the station of His vicegerent.

﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."﴾ (2:31) They said, ﴿Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise.﴾ (2:32) He said, ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names.﴾ So when he had informed them of their names, He said, ﴿Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [secrets] of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?﴾ (2:33)

After this, in Surah al-Baqarah, the prostration of the angels and the events of Iblis's refusal and arrogance are described. The story of Adam and his wife being settled in Paradise is related. Then it is told how Satan misled Adam and Eve and thus got them expelled from Paradise. After this, Adam and Eve were sent down to the earth, and here the responsibility of the duty of earthly vicegerency was placed upon them. But before their expulsion from Paradise, they were tested and prepared to live on the earth. They repented and sought forgiveness from Allah. After this story in Surah al-Baqarah, the Children of Israel are reminded to remember the blessings that I bestowed upon them, and to fulfil the covenants they made with God, because this duty is the one that Adam (peace be upon him), the father of all humankind, took upon himself, and upon that covenant was based his attainment of earthly vicegerency.

The story also appears in Surah al-A'raf. There, the long account is related that concerns his elevation in Paradise and his subsequent expulsion from there. The lesson recalled in this story is that Iblis has been the enemy of humankind from the beginning of creation and will remain so to the end, until Adam and Iblis are presented again before the divine court as they were before. One group will be those who enter Paradise, from which Satan had expelled their parents, because they opposed Satan, regarding him as their enemy. Another group will be thrown into the Fire, because they followed the steps of the accursed, arrogant Satan. For this reason, the prostration of the angels before Adam is also mentioned there, as is the mention that Iblis refused and became arrogant. He demanded of Allah that he be granted respite until the Day of Resurrection, so that he could mislead those children of Adam because of whom he had been expelled from Paradise in disgrace. Then Adam and his wife were settled in Paradise and commanded that they might eat and drink whatever they wished, but not approach one particular tree. This prohibition regarding one tree was in reality a symbolic prohibition. Its purpose was to test Adam (peace be upon him) regarding his willingness to obey the command and the strength of his will. After this, the account describes how Satan put whisperings into their hearts, how they tasted the fruit of that tree, how their bodies were miraculously uncovered, how Allah's displeasure descended upon Adam and his wife, and how they, all of them, were sent down to the earth and settled there, so that they might take part in the struggle between truth and falsehood on this earth too. It is said:

﴿[Allah] said, "Descend, some of you to others an enemy. And for you upon the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time."﴾ (7:24) ﴿He said, "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾ (7:25)

The story of humankind continues in Surah al-A'raf in this way, until all people reach the place of assembly on the Day of Resurrection again. There they speak with one another in great detail, and after argument, reckoning and accounting, one group goes into Paradise and one group into Hell.

﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or [some] of what Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers."﴾ (7:50) After this, the curtain falls on this scene.

But what is the purpose of the story here? Here the secrets of human creation and the philosophy of guidance and misguidance are under discussion, and the factors of guidance and misguidance that God has placed within the nature of humankind are examined. Therefore, the discussion here begins with the point that the human being was created from dried clay of black, decaying mud, and then Allah breathed into him His luminous spirit. Before this, Allah had created the jinn from a blazing fire. Here again the events of the prostration of the angels and Iblis's refusal appear. Iblis says: "Shall I prostrate myself before a human whom You created from clay?" Then it is shown how Satan was cursed and expelled from the divine court. Then his petition is presented, asking that he be granted respite until the Day of Resurrection. His request is granted. Here Satan admits that he will mislead people, but that he will have no power over the sincere servants of Allah. Those whom he misleads will be ready of their own accord to accept his obedience and his ways, and they will have no interest in the religion and way of Allah. The outcome of both groups is briefly stated without detail, because here the sole subject of discourse is the creation of humankind and the philosophy of guidance and misguidance.

Verses 23–25

This second paragraph is in harmony with the first. The first said:

﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.﴾ (15:23) ﴿And We certainly know those who have gone before you and We certainly know those who will come later.﴾ (15:24) "For every community that We destroyed, a specific term had been written. No nation can be destroyed before its appointed time, nor can it be spared after it." Here, however, it is decided that life and death are in Allah's hand, that Allah is the inheritor of all, and that after death people will be raised to Him. Allah knows, and He has recorded, who will be taken first, who will be granted a term of action, and who will leave this world afterwards. In any case, everyone will be raised after death and will return to Allah.

So there the secrets and mysteries of Adam's office of earthly vicegerency are explained, at which the angels were astonished, because those secrets were hidden from their view. Accordingly, Allah had to reveal to them the station of His vicegerent.

﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."﴾ (2:31) They said, ﴿Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Then it is told how Satan misled Adam and Eve and thus got them expelled from Paradise. After this, Adam and Eve were sent down to the earth, and here the responsibility of the duty of earthly vicegerency was placed upon them. The story also appears in Surah al-A'raf. There, the long account is related that concerns his elevation in Paradise and his subsequent expulsion from there. The lesson recalled in this story is that Iblis has been the enemy of humankind from the beginning of creation and will remain so to the end, until Adam and Iblis are presented again before the divine court as they were before. One group will be those who enter Paradise, from which Satan had expelled their parents, because they opposed Satan, regarding him as their enemy. Another group will be thrown into the Fire, because they followed the steps of the accursed, arrogant Satan. For this reason, the prostration of the angels before Adam is also mentioned there, as is the mention that Iblis refused and became arrogant. He demanded of Allah that he be granted respite until the Day of Resurrection, so that he could mislead those children of Adam because of whom he had been expelled from Paradise in disgrace. Then Adam and his wife were settled in Paradise and commanded that they might eat and drink whatever they wished, but not approach one particular tree. ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or [some] of what Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers."﴾ (7:50) After this, the curtain falls on this scene.

But what is the purpose of the story here? Here the secrets of human creation and the philosophy of guidance and misguidance are under discussion, and the factors of guidance and misguidance that God has placed within the nature of humankind are examined. Therefore, the discussion here begins with the point that the human being was created from dried clay of black, decaying mud, and then Allah breathed into him His luminous spirit. Here Satan admits that he will mislead people, but that he will have no power over the sincere servants of Allah. Those whom he misleads will be ready of their own accord to accept his obedience and his ways, and they will have no interest in the religion and way of Allah. The outcome of both groups is briefly stated without detail, because here the sole subject of discourse is the creation of humankind and the philosophy of guidance and misguidance.

Verses 26 to 27

At the very beginning of the story it is said that there is a distinction between the natures of humans and jinn, or Satans, from the day of the creation of the universe. Man was created from dry clay that rings, which was taken from rotted, fermented mud, meaning that when this clay is struck it rings. And Satan was created from the scorching fire of samum (the poisonous wind), or from a blazing flame or fire. Later it will become known that a new element has also entered the make-up of man: Allah has breathed into man something of His own Spirit. As for Satan, he remains upon the nature of the scorching fire.

﴿And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay, from black mud altered, dry clay. So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration." So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblees; he refused to be among the prostrators.﴾ (15:28–31)

He said, "O Iblees, what is [the reason] that you are not among the prostrators?" He said, "I am not one to prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud altered." He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled, and upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense." (15:32–35)

Now, remember the occasion when Allah spoke with the angels. When did this happen? Where did this incident take place? What was its detailed manner? We have already given the answer to these questions in the first Juz', in Surah al-Baqarah. That is, a complete answer to these questions cannot be given, because this is a story of the higher world, and we do not have any explicit text (nass sarih) about it, since we can answer any question concerning the unseen world only from an explicit text. Those who wish to answer such questions are exerting vain effort, groping in darkness, and their statements have no proof.

As for how man was created from clay that was rotted, and how, from this fermented clay, he was shaped and then somehow dried so that it rang, and then how the spirit was placed within him, we say plainly that we are unaware of the detailed modalities of these matters. In no way can we again conduct a scientific analysis of this process.

In this regard, we keep in view the verses of the Holy Qur'an that have come concerning it, especially this verse: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ (23:12). And in another verse: ﴿And We created man from an extract of fluid, despised﴾ (32:8 in Arabic numbering as cited).

From these verses it becomes known that the origin of man and the reality of life is from the clay of this earth, and that within man exist the same essential elements that are the essential constituents of this earth. Likewise, the bodies of man and of all other living beings are made of these same elements. The word sulalah (extract) points to a refined manner. Here the Qur'an indicates, and from its words this meaning is derived; but beyond this, what has been learned from the discoveries of the modern age and taken from the Qur'an is a strain (takalluf). The present verses do not bear those meanings. As for scientific research, it has its own method. Scientific research will continue with its means and resources, and the results of scientific research are hypothetical. Scientific research will continue with its means and resources, and the results of scientific research are assumptions; they are not facts but theories. Some of these theories take on the form of facts, and they too change after debate and examination; yet no result of these scientific investigations is contrary to the fundamental truths established in the Qur'an. The initial truth that the Qur'an has given is only this: that man was initially created from an extract of clay, and water forms a large part of his creation. Therefore the initial truth that the Qur'an has stated remains in its place; the theories that come later are its details.

The question is how clay and the elements of life contained in it took the form of a living human being, how the organs were formed, and how the shape and figure of man came into existence. This is the mystery whose causes and reasons humanity has been powerless to discover until today. How the first cell received life: scientists who work on human and the growth of life have not been able to learn this secret until now. As for the higher level of human life, in which the powers of understanding and insight exist, it contains distinctive powers through which man has subdued the whole universe and brought under control all other living animals. This human being has decisive superiority over this entire world. This is indeed that great mystery concerning which human theories are, until today, bewildered. Yet concerning this important mystery, the Qur'an gives man a very simple, clear and summary knowledge.

﴿...when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My soul﴾ (15:29). Indeed it is the soul created by Allah that transforms this lowly physical creature into an exalted human creature. But the important question remains: how did this happen? The answer is this reality: man has never been given the perceptive faculty by which he could comprehend this reality. Therefore the position of Muslims is that they cannot perceive this secret at all. This position is extremely firm, and we stand upon it with great contentment.

Before this, that is, before the creation of man, Allah had created Satan from the scorching fire. Satan and the satanic power existed even before the creation of Adam. This is the knowledge and certain information that Allah has given us. As for the state of satanic humiliation and the details of its creation, that is a different reality, and Allah has not made it our obligation to engage in idle debates and investigations into these fruitless matters. Yes, we do know some attributes of this fiery creation, and we know the scorching flame and blazing fire, and the fiery qualities of this power affect the human self, because they are from fire. Moreover, we know that the nature and attributes of jinn include harshness and swiftness, because their creation is from the poisonous samum wind. Also, from within this story, it is understood that Satan has the attribute of pride and arrogance; since Satan was of the jinn, pride and arrogance should be the characteristic of his temperament, because these qualities go together with fire.

Since man's creation was from rotted mud, which became dry and turned into clay (salsal), meaning that a ringing sound came from it, then into it was breathed a spirit from the Divine Being, by which this category of living creation was distinguished from other creatures. Then it was given specific human attributes, and among these attributes the important one was the human's scientific progress, which he was making in the field of humanities.

This breathing of the spirit actually connects man with the higher world. It is this attribute that gives man the capacity to draw near to God, and it is this capacity that gives man the ability to take guidance from God, so that the human rises above the world of the physical, material and senses, and works in that realm of abstraction in which heart and mind display their dash. Thus man is given that secret which he reaches in such conditions that he transcends time and place and, moving beyond the sphere of the senses, arrives at the world of unlimited conceptions.

Despite attaining these high ranks, the taint of materiality nonetheless remains with man. His temperament remains material, and he is subject to material needs and weaknesses. He eats, drinks, and needs clothing. He has natural inclinations and sexual desires. Deficiencies and shortcomings are in him, and because of his physical and imaginative weakness, bad deeds proceed from him.

The aim and lofty objective of Islam is that man, as man, should reach a high and exalted station of a beautiful balance between the demands of matter and clay and the demands of the spiritual and the higher. This is the advanced and elevated station that we call kamal basri (human perfection). Islam does not demand of man that he neglect one of his constituent elements and become purely spiritual, a monk or a Hindu, a yogi, or become a purely materialist who, by denying all higher values except material ones, becomes an animal. If man chooses only one of these two elements, he can never traverse the stages of perfection and progress. Those peoples who, keeping only one element in view, nurture man, are working against the purposes for which this creature was created.

Those who try to paralyse the physical powers of man are precisely those who want to destroy the spiritual powers of man. Both parties are going against man's straight natural temperament. Such people want to draw from man a task concerning which the Creator has made no demand. Both kinds of people are casting themselves into destruction, because they are cutting off one part of the human body; therefore they will be accountable before God in this matter, since they are committing a crime against nature.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) admonished those who expressed their intention to adopt monasticism. For example, some said that they would never approach a woman. Some said that they would fast continually and never break the fast. Someone said that he would worship through the whole night and never sleep even for a moment. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave them severe admonition. At the end of the hadith of Aishah it is said: "Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me" (fa man raghiba 'an sunnati fa laysa minni).

The rules of the Shariah that Islam has laid down for man are established on this same principle. Islam has given a code of ethics and law that is based on this principle, and in it all of man's natural capacities have been taken into account. Islam does not uproot any of man's faculties; rather, Islam establishes a kind of balance among these faculties so that no power or capacity exceeds the limit of moderation and no faculty destroys another. For, by disturbing the balance, the unbalanced faculty will in any case perish, and certain characteristics of man would cease to exist at all. Thus man would become a transgressor of the Shariah, since Allah has also commanded that you preserve your natural powers and nurture them, because they are bestowed by Allah and are for a purpose; they are not superfluous, nor are they without purpose.

These were some of the matters and thoughts that entered the heart after reflecting on the reality of human creation. The Holy Qur'an impresses upon the mind precisely these truths concerning the creation of man. Now it is appropriate that we turn to the scenes and sights of this story.

Now let us take up the scenes of this story in detail here.
