This human being has decisive superiority over this entire world. This is indeed that great mystery concerning which human theories are, until today, bewildered. Yet concerning this important mystery, the Qur'an gives man a very simple, clear and summary knowledge.

﴿...when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My soul﴾ (15:29). Indeed it is the soul created by Allah that transforms this lowly physical creature into an exalted human creature. But the important question remains: how did this happen? The answer is this reality: man has never been given the perceptive faculty by which he could comprehend this reality. Therefore the position of Muslims is that they cannot perceive this secret at all. This position is extremely firm, and we stand upon it with great contentment.

Before this, that is, before the creation of man, Allah had created Satan from the scorching fire. Satan and the satanic power existed even before the creation of Adam. This is the knowledge and certain information that Allah has given us. As for the state of satanic humiliation and the details of its creation, that is a different reality, and Allah has not made it our obligation to engage in idle debates and investigations into these fruitless matters. Yes, we do know some attributes of this fiery creation, and we know the scorching flame and blazing fire, and the fiery qualities of this power affect the human self, because they are from fire. Moreover, we know that the nature and attributes of jinn include harshness and swiftness, because their creation is from the poisonous samum wind. Also, from within this story, it is understood that Satan has the attribute of pride and arrogance; since Satan was of the jinn, pride and arrogance should be the characteristic of his temperament, because these qualities go together with fire.

Since man's creation was from rotted mud, which became dry and turned into clay (salsal), meaning that a ringing sound came from it, then into it was breathed a spirit from the Divine Being, by which this category of living creation was distinguished from other creatures. Then it was given specific human attributes, and among these attributes the important one was the human's scientific progress, which he was making in the field of humanities.

This breathing of the spirit actually connects man with the higher world. It is this attribute that gives man the capacity to draw near to God, and it is this capacity that gives man the ability to take guidance from God, so that the human rises above the world of the physical, material and senses, and works in that realm of abstraction in which heart and mind display their dash. Thus man is given that secret which he reaches in such conditions that he transcends time and place and, moving beyond the sphere of the senses, arrives at the world of unlimited conceptions.

Despite attaining these high ranks, the taint of materiality nonetheless remains with man. His temperament remains material, and he is subject to material needs and weaknesses. He eats, drinks, and needs clothing. He has natural inclinations and sexual desires. Deficiencies and shortcomings are in him, and because of his physical and imaginative weakness, bad deeds proceed from him.

The aim and lofty objective of Islam is that man, as man, should reach a high and exalted station of a beautiful balance between the demands of matter and clay and the demands of the spiritual and the higher. This is the advanced and elevated station that we call kamal basri (human perfection). Islam does not demand of man that he neglect one of his constituent elements and become purely spiritual, a monk or a Hindu, a yogi, or become a purely materialist who, by denying all higher values except material ones, becomes an animal. If man chooses only one of these two elements, he can never traverse the stages of perfection and progress. Those peoples who, keeping only one element in view, nurture man, are working against the purposes for which this creature was created.

Those who try to paralyse the physical powers of man are precisely those who want to destroy the spiritual powers of man. Both parties are going against man's straight natural temperament. Such people want to draw from man a task concerning which the Creator has made no demand. Both kinds of people are casting themselves into destruction, because they are cutting off one part of the human body; therefore they will be accountable before God in this matter, since they are committing a crime against nature.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) admonished those who expressed their intention to adopt monasticism. For example, some said that they would never approach a woman. Some said that they would fast continually and never break the fast. Someone said that he would worship through the whole night and never sleep even for a moment. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave them severe admonition. At the end of the hadith of Aishah it is said: "Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me" (fa man raghiba 'an sunnati fa laysa minni).

The rules of the Shariah that Islam has laid down for man are established on this same principle. Islam has given a code of ethics and law that is based on this principle, and in it all of man's natural capacities have been taken into account. Islam does not uproot any of man's faculties; rather, Islam establishes a kind of balance among these faculties so that no power or capacity exceeds the limit of moderation and no faculty destroys another. For, by disturbing the balance, the unbalanced faculty will in any case perish, and certain characteristics of man would cease to exist at all. Thus man would become a transgressor of the Shariah, since Allah has also commanded that you preserve your natural powers and nurture them, because they are bestowed by Allah and are for a purpose; they are not superfluous, nor are they without purpose.

These were some of the matters and thoughts that entered the heart after reflecting on the reality of human creation. The Holy Qur'an impresses upon the mind precisely these truths concerning the creation of man. Now it is appropriate that we turn to the scenes and sights of this story.

Allah said to the angels:

Verses 28–29

So the angels did exactly as Allah had commanded. And since Allah had determined to create man, as soon as the required will was exercised, man came into being. The question is: how did the spirit of Allah, which was breathed into this mortal clay body, and which is an immortal thing, become mixed with this clay body, which is mortal? A believer does not raise such questions, because debating and discussing this subject is a futile effort. Rather, to dispute and argue in such matters is merely a waste of time. By speaking on these subjects, we bring the intellect into a domain in which its means of comprehension and its power of judgment simply cannot function. The discussions held on this matter before, or being held now, are based on the ignorance in which man himself is entangled regarding the reality of human intellect. It is not the station of human intellect to step beyond its own limits and interfere in the domain of what is beyond. For the intellect does not have the power to go beyond the limits and capacity of its means of comprehension, because the nature of the Creator of the universe lies beyond the limits of human intellect. Therefore, to apply the intellect in this field is sheer foolishness. To exhaust human intellect in seeking the secrets of the creation of the universe is itself the fundamental error. The intellect cannot make any judgment as to how a mortal thing can be connected and mixed with an eternal and everlasting reality. One thing is eternal and the other originated, and Allah has not required of human intellect that it make a decision on this matter and establish it. For Allah Almighty has only told us in the Holy Quran that it happened, but nowhere has He told us how it happened or in what manner it happened. It is established that man is a created being and is present before us. Human intellect cannot deny this present reality, nor can human intellect itself describe the manner of this creation. Within the power of human intellect is only this: that it confirm the report of the Quran. As far as reaching the reality is concerned, human intellect cannot do so. And it is established by guidance that man himself and human intellect are originated, created and mortal realities, and it is also established that no mortal and created thing can pass any judgment upon eternal, everlasting and immortal realities, in any form or shape. In this matter, the well-being of the intellect lies in refraining from showing its prowess in this field and working in those fields that are open and safe for it, such as the general scientific fields.

This is because the nature of the unseen matters is of one kind, and in regard to all these unseen matters we wish to establish a principled rule with which the human heart and mind, human thought and faith, may be satisfied. In any case, what happened after this?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 30–31:

Verses 30–31

The angels prostrated because their very nature is the worship of God and the carrying out of His command, without question or hesitation. Iblis refused because he was not among the angels. The angels are a creation of light, and Satan is a creation of fire. The angels are such that whatever command they receive from God, they do not disobey it; whatever they are commanded, they carry out. Iblis, on hearing this command, immediately refused and showed arrogance (istikbar). Therefore, he was certainly not among the angels. Here the exception (istithna') is not a connected exception (istithna' muttasil). It is like the way one says: "All the children of so-and-so have come, except Ahmad has not come," when Ahmad is not one of so-and-so's sons. Rather, he is someone who lives with them, or is connected to the action of those who came. Thus there is some relation, and so he is included in the exceptive sentence.

Here the question arises: the command was given to the angels, so how did Iblis come to be included in the meaning of that command? The answer is that the context of the discourse shows that Iblis was also included in this command. In Surah al-A'raf it is explicitly stated that Iblis was included:

"Qala ma mana'aka alla tasjuda idh amartuka" ("He said: what prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?").

It is the manner of the Qur'an's expression that it is content with the contextual meaning, and this style is found abundantly in the Qur'an. The verse under discussion is decisive in indicating that Iblis too had been given a command from God, and it is not necessary that this command be the same as the one given to the angels. It is also possible that Iblis was included in the commands given to the angels, because the command related to him. And it is also possible that Iblis was given a separate command, but it is not mentioned here because the purpose here was to disregard him and to highlight the angels. However, as these verses show, Iblis was not among the angels, and we also adopt this position.

What is the reality of the angels? What is the reality of Iblis? These are unseen matters (ghaybi umur) and are among the established articles of faith (musallamat-i-imaniyah). We believe in them in the same way as they have been mentioned in the texts (nusus). As we explained above, reason has no access to these realities, so it cannot reach any reality beyond the texts. Its sphere of operation is extremely limited.

Verses 39 to 40

Here Iblis himself has determined the field of battle: that he will wage war against the children of Adam on earth.

"La-uzayyinanna lahum fi al-ardi" (I will certainly make the things of the earth appear attractive to them) — in other words, "I will make attractive for them, on earth, their own alluring things." In the same way, he has also announced the weapon he will use in this battlefield. It is this: I will make wrong and harmful deeds appear pleasing to them. I will call evil good. Through artificial beauties I will ensnare them in the net of deception. Thus, whoever commits shirk does so only because Satan makes it appear pleasing to him. He dresses evil in the garb of good, and he never presents evil in the form of evil. Regarding any thing that has been made to appear pleasing, and towards which the inclination of the human self is strong, there is a strong probability that Satan's hand lies behind such matters. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 45–48:

Verses 45 to 48

Who are the muttaqun (the God-fearing)? They are those who fear Allah and strive to protect themselves from His punishment. They keep themselves away from the causes that bring about the punishment of Allah. The gardens and the springs mentioned concerning them stand in contrast to the seven gates. These people will enter the gardens in complete peace and security, and they will not be frightened in the way the people of Hell were. The resentment that existed among them against one another, We will remove from their hearts. Whereas the envy and rancour in the heart of Iblis will remain with the people of Hell forever, and they will keep blaming one another. For the people of Paradise there will be no hardship, nor will there be any danger of their being expelled from there. These people used to fear Allah in the earth, but here there will be no fear or dread for them. They will be happy and joyful in the shade of the mercy of the Generous Lord.

Lesson No. 117: At a Glance

In this lesson there are many examples of both the mercy of Allah and the punishment of Allah. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is granted offspring despite his old age, and he is called "a son of knowledge" (Ishaq). Lut (peace be upon him) is granted salvation, and from this mercy only his wife is deprived, because her connection was with the wrongdoers. Then there is also a mention of the evil fate of the People of the Thicket (Ashab al-Aykah) and the People of al-Hijr.

All these stories and examples come after this introduction:

"Inform My servants that I am the Most Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is indeed the painful punishment" (15:49–50). Thus, among these examples and stories, some are examples of Allah's mercy and some of Allah's punishment. These stories are also relevant to the earlier commentary at the beginning of this surah, in which people were warned:

"Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let false hope distract them; they will soon come to know. We never destroyed a town except that it had a decreed term. No nation can precede its appointed time, nor can it delay it" (15:3–5). Thus these stories are examples of the towns that were destroyed, and when their term of respite ended, punishment descended upon them. Also, at the beginning of the surah it was mentioned concerning the descent of the angels that they descend with truth.

"They say, 'O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, you are surely mad. Why do you not bring us angels, if you are among the truthful?' We do not send down the angels except with truth, and then they would not be given respite" (15:6–8). Thus this surah becomes a unified and coherent theme, in which all its parts appear to be in harmony with and supportive of one another, despite the fact that the surahs were not revealed in the order in which we find them in the Mushaf. It is established, however, that the arrangement of verses within the surahs is from Allah, that is, tawqifi (divinely determined). Therefore, wisdom and order are certainly observed within this divine arrangement. Concerning the order of the subject matters of these surahs and their harmony, Allah has disclosed to us some aspects, which we have explained in the introductions to all the surahs. We have described the atmosphere of each surah and its features; true knowledge, however, belongs to Allah alone. The order, coherence of themes and wisdom that we have stated are ijtihadi (based on personal reasoning). Wallahu a'lam bis-sawab.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 49–50:

Lesson No. 117: Explanation of the Verses

49 ... to ... 84

Verses 49 to 50

Immediately after the mention of the punishment of the misguided and the reward of those who follow the guidance, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to proclaim this matter. Its connection within the context of the discourse is evident. Here, the proclamation of mercy and forgiveness is placed first, and the announcement of punishment is mentioned afterwards, because it is the pleasure of Allah that people attain His mercy and forgiveness, since Allah has made mercy and forgiveness binding upon Himself. However, at times, according to the demands of the theme and the occasion, only the punishment is mentioned, or both are mentioned but, because of some particular wisdom in the context, the mention of Allah's punishment comes first. Its explanation has also been given in such places.

After this comes the story of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the angels who were sent to destroy the people of Lut. The story of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) has come in the Qur'an at several places, and everywhere it has been presented in a different style. In accordance with the context of each place, one part of this story has been taken. Indeed, the story of Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) has also come separately at some places.

A part of the story of Lut has already passed in Surah al-A'raf. Then, in Surah Hud, the story of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) has also been mentioned. In Surah al-A'raf, there was a mention of Prophet Lut's (peace be upon him) reproach and rebuke of his people for their indecency, and the reply given by the people to his reproach was:

﴿Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who pose as pure.﴾ But when the punishment of Allah came, Allah saved him and his family, except for his wife, who remained among those who stayed behind. Here, the arrival of the angels and the whisperings of the people about them were not mentioned.

In Surah Hud, this story includes the mention of the angels. The accounts of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) are given, but the manner of narration differs everywhere. There, certain details are specific to Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him): his wife was standing and was hearing the good news from the angels. Then Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) began to argue with the angels about Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) and the people of Lut. These links have been omitted here. The sequence of events concerning Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) is also different. In the events narrated in Surah Hud, the reality of the angels was kept hidden. Their reality became apparent to him when people came running, having heard of Prophet Lut's (peace be upon him) handsome guests, while Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) was pleading with them to spare him and his guests from disgrace, yet they would not heed him at all, until his heart was overcome and he was compelled to make this distressing statement:

﴿If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in some firm support!﴾

Here, in this story, the reality of the angels has been disclosed from the very beginning, and the matter of the people's counsel and evil intentions has been brought later, because the purpose here is not to state the sequence of events of the story, but only to show how Allah's punishment comes, and that when the angels arrive, then the period of respite for action comes to an end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 51–56:

Verses 51 to 56

When the angels came to him and said, "Peace be upon you," Ibrahim (peace be upon him) replied, "We are indeed afraid of you." Here no reason for the fear is mentioned, nor is there any mention that he brought a roasted calf and that they did not stretch out their hands to it, as is stated in Surah Hud:

﴿Then when he saw their hands not reaching towards it, he regarded them with suspicion and felt a fear within himself.﴾

Here these details are not given, because in that place the purpose of the story is that when Allah promises mercy to a people through His Messenger, that mercy certainly comes. Here, it is not intended to narrate the events of Ibrahim's story, so the good news is mentioned quickly.

﴿They said, "Do not fear. We give you the good news of a knowing boy."﴾ (15:53)

Thus the good news is given swiftly, as a bearer of good news always hastens to give it. The Qur'an, within this context, has also omitted the details and conveyed the good news directly.

Here, Ibrahim's own response, his question and his amazement, is what is mentioned, and the speech of his wife is omitted.

﴿He said, "Do you give me good news even though old age has overtaken me? Then what is this good news you give?"﴾ (15:54)

At first, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) considered it unlikely that he could be granted a child at this age, especially since another place explicitly states that he said his wife was old and barren. The angels replied:

﴿They said, "We have given you the good news in truth, so do not be among those who despair."﴾ (15:55)

Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) immediately reconsidered his position and rejected despair.

﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"﴾ (15:56)

In Ibrahim's words, the Qur'an has recorded the word "mercy," which is in deep harmony with the context and situation. His statement establishes a principle: only those who have lost the straight path despair of Allah's mercy. They have departed from the way of Allah; the pleasant breeze of divine mercy does not blow upon them; they do not realize that at every step Allah's mercies descend upon a person, and they do not understand that at every moment they are under Allah's compassion and that He protects them. In contrast, the heart that is refreshed by divine mercy, that is connected to the All-Merciful, never falls prey to despair, even if it is surrounded by trials and hardships, even if there are darknesses of affliction around it, even if clouds of despair hover over its head, and even if the path to the goal is not visible far and wide, because the mercy of Allah is always close to the hearts of the believers.

At this point, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) becomes satisfied regarding these beings, namely the angels, and he has attained complete tranquility and joy at the good news they gave. Now he asks about the real purpose and objective of the angels' coming.

Thus the good news is given swiftly, as a bearer of good news always hastens to give it. The Qur'an, within this context, has also omitted the details and conveyed the good news directly.

Here, Ibrahim's own response, his question and his amazement, is what is mentioned, and the speech of his wife is omitted.

﴿He said, "Do you give me good news even though old age has overtaken me? Then what is this good news you give?"﴾ (15:54)

At first, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) considered it unlikely that he could be granted a child at this age, especially since another place explicitly states that he said his wife was old and barren. The angels replied:

﴿They said, "We have given you the good news in truth, so do not be among those who despair."﴾ (15:55)

Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) immediately reconsidered his position and rejected despair.

﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"﴾ (15:56)

In Ibrahim's words, the Qur'an has recorded the word "mercy," which is in deep harmony with the context and situation. His statement establishes a principle: only those who have lost the straight path despair of Allah's mercy. They have departed from the way of Allah; the pleasant breeze of divine mercy does not blow upon them; they do not realize that at every step Allah's mercies descend upon a person, and they do not understand that at every moment they are under Allah's compassion and that He protects them. In contrast, the heart that is refreshed by divine mercy, that is connected to the All-Merciful, never falls prey to despair, even if it is surrounded by trials and hardships, even if there are darknesses of affliction around it, even if clouds of despair hover over its head, and even if the path to the goal is not visible far and wide, because the mercy of Allah is always close to the hearts of the believers.

At this point, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) becomes satisfied regarding these beings, namely the angels, and he has attained complete tranquility and joy at the good news they gave. Now he asks about the real purpose and objective of the angels' coming.

In the context here, it is not mentioned that Abraham (peace be upon him) argued at length with the angels about the people of Lot (peace be upon him), as is described in Surah Hud. Rather, here the angels relate the whole matter to Abraham (peace be upon him) at once, because they affirm the confirmation of the mercy of God upon Lot (peace be upon him) and the family of Lot. However, the decision concerning his wife is somewhat different: she is among those who remain behind (ghabirin, meaning those who stay behind with the people; she became one of them and her fate was the fate of the people. The word is derived from ghabirah, which is applied to the milk that remains in the udder of an animal after it has been milked). Thereupon the angels proceed toward the people of Lot.

Moreover, he was weak among his people, while the people were powerful and wicked. That is, he was saying: "You are strange people, that you have come into this village, although these people are immersed in the wickedness and debauchery, and the way they treat people like you is well known." But the angels made the matter clear:

These emphases show how helpless Lut (peace be upon him) had become in this matter and how restless his state was. He was perplexed: on one side he was responsible for his guests, and on the other he was powerless before his people. Therefore the angels gave him reassurance in the most emphatic words, and before giving him final instructions, they fully satisfied him that the time of these people had now come to an end.

Here, since the punishment was to come in the morning and the time was fixed, they were strictly urged to leave promptly.

This manner of expression indicates their complete annihilation. Therefore the Muslims were strictly instructed that none of them should look back, lest, like the disbelievers, they also be caught in the punishment, for how could those left behind escape the general punishment?

This passage from Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on the Qur'an, surah 15, verse 67, is an Urdu text. Note: the instruction-free tail is fine; here is the translation.

The manner of expression shows that these people had crossed all limits of wickedness (fisq), immorality (fujur), indecency (fuhsh) and shamelessness, and that this entire people was morally diseased. How strange and shameful is this scene: people coming in groups, rejoicing, and openly saying that today a good catch has come into their hands. On the one hand there is evil and waywardness; on the other, it is being done openly and brazenly. No healthy human society could even imagine such a thing. An individual may occasionally adopt such behaviour, but even he conceals his sickness. He may obtain this misguided pleasure secretly and save himself from shame before people. But for an entire society to do it openly is something else, because even a sound-natured person who enjoys sexual pleasure within lawful limits does so in private. Some animals too conceal sexual union, yet look at these people: like those going to a fair or festival, they go openly for this indecency, demand it openly, declare their intention, and come for this purpose in a collective form. This is a state for which there is no parallel in the history of human society.

In these circumstances, in a state of utter helplessness, Hadrat Lut (ʿalayhi al-salam) stands in a state of extreme anguish and distress. He strives to save his guests and his own honour. He appeals to them by human nobility and human values, he warns them of God, and he invokes the name of Allah, although he knows that the hearts of these people are devoid of the fear of God. He knows that these people have no sense of humanity, no human consciousness, and nothing within them called fear of God and taqwa. Yet even in this state of distress he makes his final effort, appealing to them by humanity, saying that these are guests, and warning them that their intentions are against the command of God. In any case, he strives.

Verses 68–69

The earnest appeal of Lut (peace be upon him), instead of stirring any human feeling in their hearts or making them feel ashamed, only made them become even more brazen in their response. They themselves began to rebuke Lut (peace be upon him), saying that he brings to his house guests of this sort, who are for our purpose. As if the guilty party were not they, but rather Lut (peace be upon him) himself, since he was bringing before them a prey against which they could not exercise any restraint over themselves.

But Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) continues to show them the path of the sound human nature. He draws their attention to the fact that the Creator of life has arranged things in a particular way. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verse 71:

Verse No. 71

Hazrat Lut (peace be upon him) was a Prophet. He was not presenting his own daughters to those debauchees so that they might commit immorality with them. Rather, he was directing them towards the women of the people, [pointing out] that Allah had created these women for this very purpose. And this is the natural and healthy path. Lut himself knew that their demand was not that they commit immorality with his daughters; rather, they had abandoned the natural path and adopted deviation.

This was the scene before us: the people of Lut, with their diseased mentality, were engaged in lighthearted chatter, and the intention of evil was being expressed through hints and innuendo. Meanwhile, Hazrat Lut (peace be upon him) was busy defending the guests; he was trying to awaken their unslumbering conscience. He was trying to awaken their conscience and intuition, and to seek out in them the inclination of sound human nature, while they kept advancing in their base intention.

This scene was playing on the screen in this way when suddenly, in the manner of pure Arabic speech, a comment arrives on the conflict between Lut (peace be upon him) and the people of Lut, and the address begins with an oath:

This was their true picture, and in that state they always remained. Therefore, despite Lut's (peace be upon him) efforts, he had no hope that they would come onto the right path, nor any expectation that feelings of decency and honour would awaken within them, or that they would fear God and return to the straight path and the sound nature.

Now the time of their end is drawing near, and the word of Allah is coming true.

﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and at that time they would not be given respite﴾ (15:8) "And We do not send the angels except with truth, and then they are not given respite." Now before us comes the final scene. This is a scene of destruction, ruin and being swallowed up into the earth. It is an all-encompassing devastation visible on every side.

Commentary on Verses 73–74

The punishment that came upon the people of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) appears to resemble a severe earthquake and volcanic eruption, in which entire settlements sink into the earth, in which there is also a rain of stones, and in which there are also stones of baked clay. It was an all-encompassing destruction. It is said that the Dead Sea (Bahr-e-Lut) emerged after this all-encompassing calamity, at the time when the entire population of Sodom (Sadum) sank into the earth, and in that place so large a pit appeared that water collected there and became a sea.

The settlements of the people of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) were located on the public highway on the route from the Hijaz to Syria, and any intelligent and perceptive person can take a lesson from observing them. However, all these signs and indications are beneficial only for those hearts which have the capacity, which are open to guidance, and in which true faith and convictions are present.

Therefore, the denial of one was counted as the denial of all. When they denied him, it was said that they denied all the messengers, because the messenger and the message are one institution. They have presented one and the same doctrine in every era and every age. Despite differences of time and place, they were one.

"And We gave them Our signs, but they kept turning away from them" (15:81). "We sent Our signs to them, but they persisted in turning away." The sign and miracle of Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) was the she-camel, yet the word "signs" is used in the plural rather than the singular because besides the she-camel, other signs are scattered throughout this universe. There are many signs even within the human self. All these signs invite our reflection. If they denied one miracle of Prophet Salih (peace be upon him), then in reality they denied all the miracles scattered throughout this universe. They did not try to understand the signs spread around them. They kept shut the doors of their conscience and their awareness.

"And they used to carve houses out of the mountains and were secure" (15:82). "Then the blast seized them at morning" (15:83). "So what they had earned did not avail them" (15:84). "They carved houses out of the mountains and were feeling completely fearless and secure in their place. At last a terrible blast overtook them at the very break of morning, and what they had earned did not avail them." This moment came to them suddenly. These people were sitting safely inside the houses carved out of the mountain. Whatever they had earned for their protection, whatever strong buildings they had constructed, and whatever secure dwellings they had made by cutting into the mountains, none of it was of any use to them. A terrible blast occurred, and afterwards there was nothing left at all in those settlements. This moment leaves deep effects upon human consciousness. No more secure refuge can even be imagined than those who make shelters for themselves by cutting into mountains and rocks. Then, when a person passes the night and enters the morning, he bids farewell to the night with great calm and without fear, but in those reassuring moments of morning they were struck by a terrible blast, and they lost everything along with their precious lives. All their precautionary measures came to an end, and their secure fortresses proved to be heaps of sand. Nothing remained behind that thunderous blast. It was a sharp wind, or a violent cry, and by its effect these people became heaps of corpses within their most secure homes.

In this way, this surah casts a brief glance over historical narratives and events, and from all these stories it gives only this lesson: when the respite granted by God comes to an end and the time of a nation's ruin arrives, then in accordance with the Divine Way the punishment of God comes, the angels descend with truth, and the Divine Way does not grant even a moment's respite. This lesson is the common thread of all these narratives, and because of it all these events are interconnected.

Lesson 118: At a Glance

These are the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) from which no deviation is possible. This universe runs in accordance with these laws and ordinances of Allah. It is these same laws and ordinances that control the cosmos and life. They also control communities and movements. The consequences of guidance and misguidance likewise emerge in accordance with these divine ordinances. The fate of nations and the reckoning of the Hereafter also take place according to these natural laws. Every lesson of this surah concludes in accordance with these natural laws and the divine sunnah, and presents the divine sunnah in various styles. These natural laws exist within all of Allah's creation, and this is the truth, and the natural order of the universe stands upon this truth.

Accordingly, at the conclusion of this surah this great truth is clarified and stated. This truth is evident in the nature of the heavens and the earth and of all existents between them: that the Hour is going to come to pass. This is the natural end of this universe, and there is no room for doubt about it; and that the mission of all the Messengers is one and is in accordance with this natural law. The common quality among all the Messengers is that they bear one great truth, which is clear. Here it is explained that this truth exists within all creation, and Allah alone is the Creator of this truth.

Indeed your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing (15:86): "Surely your Lord is the Creator of all and knows everything." Therefore this truth should advance, and the Islamic call founded upon this truth should advance. The bearers of the truth should not care about anyone and should move forward. And they should not care about the opponents of the call and those who mock.

So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists (15:94): "Declare clearly what you are commanded, and ignore the polytheists." The sunnah of Allah also proceeds along its path; it has not retreated even a single step. Behind the sunnah of Allah stands a truth, and this truth is linked with the Islamic call, the establishment of the Resurrection, and the creation of the earth. This truth relates to all the things that exist in the heavens and the earth, and which are the creation of the All-Knowing Creator. This is a reminder and a warning with which this surah concludes, and this warning directs man to that great truth upon which this existence stands.

Verses 85 to 86

The statement that the heavens and the earth were created with truth is a great and important observation: that the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them were created with truth. This manner of expression is also remarkable, that all existents were not created upon any law other than truth. The question is: what is the real meaning of this phrase?

And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth (15:85): "We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except upon truth." The meaning is that truth has a deep role in the creation of this universe. This truth lies in the depths of the universe. Truth is present in the pattern of the universe's movement. The end and conclusion of the universe too will be upon truth.

In the existence of this universe there is truth, and in its planning and in its blueprint of creation there is truth; that is, it was not created as a mere game or amusement. Nor did this universe come into being by chance. In its original design and plan there is neither deception nor fraud, neither defect, nor is it a false creation. If falsehood appears to dominate it outwardly, that is superficial; falsehood is not among the real elements of this universe.

The truth is very deeply embedded in the structure of this universe. Its constituent elements are those that are the constituent elements of truth. In it there is neither illusion nor deceit. The laws that hold the elements of the universe together are based on truth, and these laws never deviate. They do not change, nor are they subject to disorder. There is no confusion or chaos in them.

The management and control of this universe rests upon very profound regulations, and it is being run with truth. The ordinances and laws established for running this universe are correct and just.

Even in the outcome of this universe, truth is deeply rooted. All the results of this universe appear in accordance with very firm laws. Whatever change and transformation occurs among the heavens, the earth and the things between them, occurs with truth. Whatever change and transformation occurs among the heavens, the earth and the things between them, occurs with truth and for the sake of truth. Every event and every principle of reward and punishment in this universe is in accordance with the sunnah of Allah, and no event occurs contrary to the sunnah of Allah.

This is why the Hour, which will most certainly come to pass, is the result of this very truth, because the universe was created with truth; therefore the Hour must occur one day, and it cannot be averted. Because the law upon which this universe stands and continues to move requires that a day of Resurrection come. This is truth in itself. When the Resurrection is truth, its occurrence is also truth.

So overlook with gracious forgiveness (15:85): "So forgive with fair forgiveness." Do not constrict your heart, do not harbour hatred or enmity toward anyone, because truth will in any case prevail as truth.

Indeed your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing (15:86): "Surely your Lord is the Creator of all and knows everything." He is the Creator; He knows what He created and why He created it. Since He created everything, truth is deposited in the nature of every thing. Therefore, just as the world began with truth, so it will end with truth, because truth is the real nature of this universe, and everything other than truth is falsehood, defect, and perishable, while truth alone remains living, radiant and eternal, deposited within the heart of the universe.

The message that the Messengers have brought is also a part of this cosmic truth, and its manifestation is in the form of the Qur'an, which was given to the Prophet (ﷺ).

The Seven Oft-Repeated (Sab' al-Mathani) — what are they? The more preferred view is that they are the seven verses of Surah al-Fatihah, as is also reported in the traditions. They are called mathani (oft-repeated) because they are repeated again and again in the prayer, or they are called so because they contain the praise of Allah. The "Great Quran" refers to the rest of the Quran.

An important point here is that in this verse the Great Quran is brought together in one thread with the signs of the creation of the universe and the signs of the occurrence of the Day of Resurrection. The purpose is to show that the creation of the universe, the establishment of the Resurrection and the revelation of the Quran are links of that one truth which is the soul of this entire universe. In this way the Quran inclines hearts to understand that great truth and the laws of nature (nawamis-e-qudrat) which are hidden in this universe, present within the human self and in the horizons. In accordance with them, people attain guidance and misguidance. The outcome of truth and falsehood, the values of good and evil, and the determination of righteousness and corruption are made according to this law of truth. This Quran comprises the articles and principles of that real truth, and through the Quran alone we can learn what the truth is on which the universe is established. In other words, the truth on which this universe has been founded is the Holy Quran. Through it the laws of nature are established, and it is linked with and arranged according to those laws of nature. This Quran is not a temporary thing, nor a reality that passes away. It is the truth, and it will always remain effective. It will continue to guide life, even if the mockers keep on mocking and scoffing, and even if the proponents of falsehood raise the banners of falsehood, because falsehood is perishable and will one day be erased.

Those to whom Surah al-Fatihah was given and this Great Quran was given, which comprises the great truth of this universe and is closely connected with that great truth and the Supreme Truth, their gaze becomes so lofty that they no longer even raise their eyes to look at false and perishable things in this world. They have no concern with the clamor of the proponents of falsehood. They do not regard it as important whether they are few or many, whether their number is small or large. Such people nevertheless keep walking on their path, because the truth is with them, and therefore their resolve remains high in every condition.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 88–89:

Verses 88–89

"Do not let your eyes stretch out." La tamuddanna ʿaynayka ila ma matta‘na bihi azwajan minhum (15:88): "Do not direct your eyes toward the worldly provision We have given to various groups among them."

In reality, the gaze does stretch and widen, but the expression of greedy looking is phrased as though the eyes have come out and grown long. This is a wonderfully astonishing and vivid picture of imagination. The meaning is: O Messenger, do not even pay attention to these things, do not give them importance. The wealth given to some men, women and classes is of no real significance.

Do not look at these things with excessive interest. Do not consider them beautiful, lest your gaze be dazzled by them and you begin to long for them. These are things that pass away; they are not the truth but falsehood, whereas you, O Messenger, are the bearer of the great truth, the oft-repeated verses (al-mathani) and the mighty Quran.

This does not mean that the deprived classes should be left in their deprivation in the world, while the wealthy and luxury-loving people are left immersed and intoxicated in their riches, while higher values are effaced, economic justice is ended, and the world is permanently divided between the deprived and the affluent (mutrafin). Islam, which is founded upon truth and which teaches that truth is the soul of this universe, how could it permit the continuation of such an oppressive and unjust situation?

Here there is a specific local meaning. The intent is that the guidance and right direction given to you is more precious than the glittering life and wealth of these people. Therefore, disregard these capitalists and turn your attention to the sincere believers, for these believers, although they may be poor by worldly standards, are the bearers of the truth upon which this universe was created, and upon which all the things existing within this universe were created. Worldly people, however, are followers of falsehood, which is a transient thing and has no connection with the true reality of this universe.

"And do not grieve over them." Wa la tahzan ʿalayhim (15:88): "And do not let your heart grieve over them." Do not worry that the end of these people will appear dreadful. On the Day of Resurrection this evil end is the demand of the truth; so leave them to their own state.

"And lower your wing to the believers." Wakhfid janahaka lil-mu’minin (15:88): "And lower your wings to the believers." Here gentleness, love and compassion are expressed in the manner of a bird spreading its wings over its young. This is an extremely graphic mode of expression, and the Quran uses it very frequently. It is a distinctive artistic style of the Holy Quran.

"And say: I am indeed the plain warner." Wa qul innI ana an-nadhir al-mubin (15:89): "And say: I am only a clear warner." The effective and genuine method of calling people is to speak clearly. Here, since the context was of deniers and mockers, only warning is mentioned; glad tidings are set aside, because the address was to those who are worldly-minded and do not reflect upon the truth that is the foundation of the creation of the universe, upon which the Quran was revealed and according to which the Resurrection will take place.

On the occasion of mention of the great truth of the creation of the universe, and of al-Fatihah and the mighty Quran, it is also made clear here that some of the opponents of the earlier messengers do not reflect upon the Holy Quran. They accept some of its teachings and reject others. They accept those matters of the Quran which agree with their books, and they do not accept those which are more numerous, although the Holy Quran is the final and complete Book of Allah, and in it have been gathered all the truths on which the earlier books were based.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 15, verses 90–93:

Verses 90–93

That is, We have given you the seven oft-repeated verses (al-Sab' al-Mathani) and the Great Quran. This is the same kind of warning that We sent down to those who divided [the Scripture] into parts. You were not the only Prophet to whom a Book was given; other Prophets too were given Books, and the Book (Umm al-Kitab) is the origin of all those Books. It is singular, its reference is one, because all the Books were sent down by Allah. Therefore, those upon whom a Book was sent down before, they have no right to deny any Book, because the True Creator, who sends down the Book, knows very well what kind of code people need in which age.

These people who have made the Quran into pieces and divided it up, accepting one part and rejecting the other part ('Adin is the plural of 'Adi, meaning a part; 'Adi al-Shah means the separation of its limbs). They opposed the attitude that was expected of them on account of being People of the Book.

﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ (15:92–93). The purpose of questioning is known, namely, punishment. When the matter reaches this point, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is addressed directly: that you (ﷺ) should continue on your path, and should openly declare the command that Allah has given you. Here the word used for this is *sad'* (ṣadʿ), whose literal meaning is to split or cleave, that is, to speak with full force. The polytheism of the people and their insistence upon it should not stop you from your struggle, because the polytheists and enemies of Islam will soon come to know their end. Likewise, today, those who mock the Islamic movement will also reach their end. Do not allow their ridicule to affect the pace of the Islamic call.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, after all, a human being and a mortal. When he saw people persisting in disbelief and polytheism, and mocking those who called them to the truth, he would become extremely angry, and he would be deeply distressed and troubled. Upon this, he was commanded to keep glorifying and praising Allah, to keep worshipping Allah, and to remain engaged in tasbih (glorification), tahlil (declaring the oneness of Allah), worship, and dhikr (remembrance) and contemplation. He was to bear the mockery and ridicule that came from the people, and to keep remembering Allah throughout his entire life, until ﴿certainty﴾ came to him, that is, death came, and he reached the sanctuary of mercy of his Lord.

Upon this, he was commanded to keep glorifying and praising Allah, to keep worshipping Allah, and to remain engaged in tasbih (glorification), tahlil (declaring the oneness of Allah), worship, and dhikr (remembrance) and contemplation. He was to bear the mockery and ridicule that came from the people, and to keep remembering Allah throughout his entire life, until ﴿certainty﴾ came to him, that is, death came, and he reached the sanctuary of mercy of his Lord.

This is the conclusion of the surah: turning away from the disbelievers, returning to the Lord, and the fact that a day is soon to come when these disbelievers will wish that they had been Muslims.
